basics.name: Jeremy Meese
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer
basics.summary: Passionate about solving complex problems with well-designed, scalable systems. I have built my career working across a diverse range of technologies—from Azure product development and big data engineering to web API design, CI/CD, and data visualization. My expertise spans C#, ASP.NET Core, SQL, Kusto, TypeScript, Entra ID, experimentation frameworks, Swagger, and visualization tools like Power BI and R with ggplot2.

work.summary: Tech lead of Azure Communication Services Resource Provider, building secure, scalable infrastructure across global and sovereign Azure clouds.
highlights: Architected and delivered high-availability control/data plane services aligned with Microsoft’s Secure Future Initiative.
Reduced service cost by 80% through strategic data restructuring and optimization.
Owned CI/CD pipelines, credential flows (Managed Identity, certificates, Federated Identity), and TypeScript-based Azure Portal UX.
Generated and maintained JavaScript SDKs, integrating with partner teams to support evolving ACS features.
work.name: Microsoft - Azure Communication Services

work.summary: Drove quality and observability efforts for the Windows Search Indexer, used by millions of devices.
highlights: Built telemetry pipelines and Docker-based enrichment tools to process petabytes of device data.
Correlated system health with real-world usage profiles via device census integration.
Identified regressions and prioritized bugs using automated crash data (Watson).
Accelerated feature iteration through robust monitoring and early fault detection.
work.name: Microsoft - Windows Search

work.summary: Focused on performance and reliability of the Windows composition stack through data-driven analysis.
highlights: Built and maintained telemetry pipelines to monitor feature-level reliability.
Integrated R and ggplot for agile regression analysis.
Used kernel debugging and crash dump analysis to detect platform-level issues.
Delivered dashboards and data workflows reused across multiple Windows releases.
